consensus_summary: The good news of salvation accomplished through Jesus Christ, centrally focused on his death for sins, burial, and resurrection, as well as the inauguration of the Kingdom of God.
book_summary: The message of the coming kingdom and the law going forth from Zion, spanning from Abraham and Mount Sinai to its renewal under Jesus.
consensus_core_identification: Salvation through Christ's death and resurrection.
book_core_identification: The promise of the coming kingdom and the law going forth from Zion.
boundary_disagreement: The consensus views the gospel primarily as the New Testament proclamation of Christ's historical death and resurrection. The book applies it to the covenantal promises given to Abraham and the law given at Mount Sinai, treating Jesus' ministry as a renewal of this earlier message.
material_contradiction: The consensus identifies the core content of the gospel as the atonement (Christ's death and resurrection for sins). The book explicitly contrasts with this 'commonly taught' view, redefining the gospel's core content as the coming kingdom and the dissemination of the law from Zion.
rationale: The book acknowledges the consensus view in its note but deliberately shifts the definition away from the events of the cross and resurrection, centering the gospel instead on the kingdom and the law, and tracing its primary declaration back to Abraham and Sinai.
strongest_objection: In 1 Corinthians 15:1-4, Paul explicitly defines the gospel he delivered as of 'first importance': that Christ died for our sins, was buried, and was raised on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures.
